topics.title: Opinion essay
topics.blurb: Agree or disagree: take a clear position and defend it in every paragraph.

swaps.plainSentence: A lot of people think that university education should be free for all students.
swaps.formalSentence: It is widely held that university education should be free for all students.
swaps.note: Report the view impersonally before giving your own.

swaps.plainSentence: Nowadays, many governments have increased their spending on public transport.
swaps.formalSentence: In recent years, many governments have increased their spending on public transport.
swaps.note: Pair 'In recent years' with the present perfect.

swaps.plain: something people argue a lot about
swaps.plainSentence: Whether zoos should be closed is something people argue a lot about.
swaps.formalSentence: Whether zoos should be closed is a highly controversial issue.

traps.why: wrong form: 'arguing' is not an adjective
idiom too informal for an essay

swaps.note: Frame the topic as a debate, then give your view.

swaps.plainSentence: I think that free public transport would bring more benefits than drawbacks.
swaps.formalSentence: I firmly believe that free public transport would bring more benefits than drawbacks.

traps.text: In my point of view I think

swaps.note: Thesis sentence: make your position unmistakable.

swaps.plainSentence: For the reasons outlined below, I totally agree with this proposal.
swaps.formalSentence: For the reasons outlined below, I wholeheartedly agree with this proposal.
swaps.note: Strong agreement: 'wholeheartedly agree with this view'.

swaps.plainSentence: Although this policy has some merit, I agree with it only a bit.
swaps.formalSentence: Although this policy has some merit, I agree with it only to a limited extent.
swaps.note: Partial agreement answers 'to what extent' precisely.

formal: The most compelling reason for this view is that
The primary justification for this view is that
swaps.plainSentence: The first thing is that free public transport would reduce the number of cars on the roads.
swaps.formalSentence: The most compelling reason for this view is that free public transport would reduce the number of cars on the roads.

traps.text: The most compelled reason is that

swaps.note: Open Body 1 with your strongest reason.

swaps.plainSentence: To start, a university degree greatly improves a graduate's job prospects.
swaps.formalSentence: To begin with, a university degree greatly improves a graduate's job prospects.
swaps.note: 'At first' describes time, not the first argument.

swaps.plainSentence: Many city centres are gridlocked because of the growing number of private cars.
swaps.formalSentence: Many city centres are gridlocked owing to the growing number of private cars.

traps.why: needs a clause, not a noun phrase

swaps.note: Owing to / as a result of + noun, never + clause.

swaps.plainSentence: Exhaust fumes are bad for the health of city residents.
swaps.formalSentence: Exhaust fumes are detrimental to the health of city residents.
swaps.note: Detrimental always takes 'to'.

swaps.plainSentence: Like, in Luxembourg, public transport has been free since 2020.
swaps.formalSentence: For instance, in Luxembourg, public transport has been free since 2020.
swaps.note: 'Like' as a filler is spoken English.

swaps.plainSentence: So, commuters would spend far less time stuck in traffic.
swaps.formalSentence: Consequently, commuters would spend far less time stuck in traffic.
swaps.note: Close a body paragraph with the result of your reason.

swaps.plainSentence: Building more roads would only make the problem worse by encouraging people to drive.
swaps.formalSentence: Building more roads would only exacerbate the problem by encouraging people to drive.
swaps.note: Exacerbate already means 'make worse'.

swaps.plainSentence: Also, free public transport would benefit low-income families the most.
swaps.formalSentence: Furthermore, free public transport would benefit low-income families the most.
swaps.note: Open Body 2 by adding a second, separate argument.

swaps.plainSentence: Another good point is that people would have more money to spend in local businesses.
swaps.formalSentence: A further advantage is that people would have more money to spend in local businesses.

traps.text: One more good thing is that

swaps.note: 'Good point' → advantage / benefit / merit.

swaps.plainSentence: Free travel would help the integration of elderly people into community life.
swaps.formalSentence: Free travel would facilitate the integration of elderly people into community life.
swaps.note: Facilitate + noun (not + person + to-infinitive).

swaps.plainSentence: Lots of elderly people rarely leave their homes because of the cost of travel.
swaps.formalSentence: A considerable number of elderly people rarely leave their homes because of the cost of travel.
swaps.note: Number + countable nouns; amount + uncountable nouns.

swaps.plainSentence: Affordable transport is very important for a fair and inclusive society.
swaps.formalSentence: Affordable transport is crucial for a fair and inclusive society.
swaps.note: Never put 'very' before crucial, vital or essential.

formal: enhance the quality of life for
improve the quality of life for
swaps.plainSentence: Such a policy would make life better for millions of urban residents.
swaps.formalSentence: Such a policy would enhance the quality of life for millions of urban residents.

traps.text: enhancing the quality of life for

swaps.note: Enhance / improve + the quality of life.

swaps.plainSentence: This shows that the social benefits would justify the financial cost.
swaps.formalSentence: This highlights that the social benefits would justify the financial cost.
swaps.note: End Body 2 by linking the example back to your thesis.

swaps.plainSentence: To sum up, I believe that free public transport is a policy worth pursuing.
swaps.formalSentence: In conclusion, I believe that free public transport is a policy worth pursuing.
swaps.note: Restate your position; add no new arguments.

swaps.plainSentence: Although there are some bad points, such as the cost to taxpayers, the advantages are far greater.
swaps.formalSentence: Although there are certain drawbacks, such as the cost to taxpayers, the advantages are far greater.
swaps.note: 'Bad point' → drawback / disadvantage.

swaps.plainSentence: In my view, the advantages of the policy are much bigger than its costs.
swaps.formalSentence: In my view, the advantages of the policy far outweigh its costs.
swaps.note: X outweighs Y: no 'than', no preposition.

formal: would be well advised to consider
swaps.plainSentence: Governments should really think about introducing it in major cities.
swaps.formalSentence: Governments would be well advised to consider introducing it in major cities.
swaps.note: A measured recommendation makes a strong final sentence.

rewrites.plain: Nowadays a lot of people think that university should be free for everyone.
rewrites.best: In recent years, it has been widely argued that university education should be free for all students.
rewrites.tooPlain: Nowadays, many people think that university should be free for everybody.
rewrites.broken: In nowadays, it is widely believing that university should be free for all.

rewrites.plain: I totally agree with this because it has lots of good points.
rewrites.best: I wholeheartedly agree with this view, as the policy offers a number of significant advantages.
rewrites.tooPlain: I really agree with this because it has many good points.
rewrites.broken: I am very agree with this view because it has many advantage.

rewrites.plain: Also, cars are bad for the environment and make pollution worse.
rewrites.best: Furthermore, private cars are detrimental to the environment and exacerbate air pollution.
rewrites.tooPlain: Also, cars are harmful to the environment and make pollution worse.
rewrites.broken: Furthermore, cars are detrimental for the environment and exacerbate pollution worse.

rewrites.plain: For example, some cities in Europe like Tallinn have made buses free for the people who live there.
rewrites.best: For instance, several European cities, such as Tallinn, have made public transport free for residents.
rewrites.tooPlain: For example, some European cities like Tallinn have made buses free for residents.
rewrites.broken: For instance, several European cities, such like Tallinn, have made free the public transport for residents.
rewrites.brokenWhy: 'such like' is wrong; word order is unnatural

rewrites.plain: But some people say it costs too much money.
rewrites.best: Nevertheless, critics contend that such a scheme would place an excessive burden on public finances.
rewrites.tooPlain: However, some people say that it costs too much.
rewrites.tooPlainWhy: 'people say' and 'costs too much' are plain
rewrites.broken: Nevertheless, critics are contending that the scheme would be too much expensive for public finances.

rewrites.plain: To sum up, the good points are bigger than the bad points.
rewrites.best: In conclusion, I believe that the advantages of this policy far outweigh its drawbacks.
rewrites.tooPlain: In conclusion, the good points are more than the bad points.
rewrites.tooPlainWhy: 'good / bad points' and 'more than' are plain
rewrites.broken: In conclusion, the advantages are far outweigh than the disadvantages.

rewrites.plain: The government should do this soon because it will help a lot of people.
rewrites.best: Governments should therefore implement this policy without delay, as it would benefit a considerable number of citizens.
rewrites.tooPlain: The government should do this soon because it will help many people.
rewrites.tooPlainWhy: 'do this' and 'help many people' are vague
rewrites.broken: Governments should implement this policy without delay, as it would beneficial a considerable number of citizens.
rewrites.brokenWhy: 'beneficial' is an adjective, not a verb

report.question: Some people believe that public transport in cities should be free of charge for everyone who uses it. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

steps.best: In recent years, it has been proposed in a number of countries that public transport in urban areas should be made free of charge for all passengers, regardless of their income.

others.text: Some people believe that public transport in cities should be free of charge for everyone who uses it.
others.why: copies the question word for word

others.text: In this modern era, public transport is a hot topic that everyone is talking about.
others.why: cliché; does not paraphrase the question

steps.best: I wholeheartedly agree with this proposal, since I believe that its environmental and social benefits would far outweigh the financial cost to governments.

others.text: I will discuss both sides of this question in this essay.
others.why: no clear position for 'to what extent'

others.text: I am totally agree with this idea because it is good.
others.why: 'am agree' is wrong; the reason is vague

steps.best: The most compelling argument in favour of free public transport is that it would significantly reduce the number of private cars on city roads.

others.text: The first reason is that cars are bad.
Firstly of all, free transport can reduce cars in the roads.
others.why: 'Firstly of all' and 'in the roads' are wrong

steps.best: At present, many city centres are heavily congested owing to commuters' reliance on cars, and the resulting exhaust fumes are highly detrimental to the health of local residents.

others.text: Now many cities have a lot of traffic because of cars and it is bad for health.
Presently, city centres are congesting due to cars, which is detrimental for health.

steps.prompt: Give an example and link back
steps.best: For instance, after Tallinn abolished fares for its residents in 2013, passenger numbers increased, which suggests that cost is a powerful incentive for drivers to leave their cars at home.

others.text: For example, Tallinn made it free and more people used it.
Such as Tallinn, which made transport free, and passengers were increased.
others.why: 'Such as' cannot start a sentence; wrong passive

steps.prompt: Topic sentence: a second, separate reason
steps.best: Furthermore, free travel would be an effective means of reducing inequality, as low-income households spend a disproportionate share of their earnings on getting to work.

others.text: Also, poor people would like it because they don't have much money.
Moreover, free travel will reduce the inequality because poor families spends a lot.

steps.best: Removing fares would facilitate access to education, employment and healthcare, thereby enhancing the quality of life of some of the most vulnerable members of society.

others.text: It would help people go to school, work and hospital and make their lives better.
Removing fares would facilitate to access education and enhance the life quality better.

steps.best: Admittedly, such a scheme would be costly; however, much of this expense could be offset by lower spending on road maintenance and on treating pollution-related illnesses.

others.text: It costs a lot, but that's OK because we save money in other ways.
Admittedly, the scheme is expensive; nevertheless of this, costs could offset by savings.

steps.best: In conclusion, I firmly believe that making urban public transport free is a sensible policy, as it would ease congestion, cut pollution and promote social equality.

others.text: To sum up, I think free transport is a good idea.
In conclusion, free transport has both advantages and disadvantages, so it depends.

steps.best: Although the initial cost would be considerable, the long-term benefits far outweigh it, and governments would be well advised to introduce such schemes in their major cities.

others.text: The good points are bigger than the bad points, so governments should do it.
Although the cost is considerable, but the benefits are far outweighing it.

topics.title: Discuss both views
topics.blurb: Present each side fairly, then say which view you support and why.

swaps.plainSentence: People have different ideas about when children should start formal schooling.
swaps.formalSentence: Opinions are divided on when children should start formal schooling.
swaps.note: Signal immediately that there are two sides.

swaps.plainSentence: Some people say that an early start gives children an academic advantage.
swaps.formalSentence: Some contend that an early start gives children an academic advantage.
swaps.note: Vary reporting verbs: argue, contend, maintain, claim.

swaps.plainSentence: This essay will talk about both views before giving my own opinion.
swaps.formalSentence: This essay will examine both views before giving my own opinion.
swaps.note: Discuss / examine + object directly: no 'about'.

swaps.plainSentence: Although both sides have good points, I believe that a later start is preferable.
swaps.formalSentence: Although both views have merit, I believe that a later start is preferable.
swaps.note: Acknowledge both sides, then commit to one.

swaps.plainSentence: Personally, I agree more with the second view.
swaps.formalSentence: Personally, I agree more with the latter view.
swaps.note: Two items: the former (first), the latter (second).

swaps.plainSentence: People who support early schooling believe that young children learn remarkably quickly.
swaps.formalSentence: Proponents of early schooling believe that young children learn remarkably quickly.
swaps.note: Name the group holding the first view.

swaps.plainSentence: On one side, an early start may give children a head start in literacy.
swaps.formalSentence: On the one hand, an early start may give children a head start in literacy.
swaps.note: Pairs with 'On the other hand' in Body 2.

swaps.plain: The reason they think this is that
formal: The reasoning behind this view is that
swaps.plainSentence: The reason they think this is that the brain is most receptive before the age of seven.
swaps.formalSentence: Their rationale is that the brain is most receptive before the age of seven.
swaps.note: Explain the logic behind the view, not just the view.

swaps.plainSentence: Children who start early get basic reading and counting skills sooner.
swaps.formalSentence: Children who start early acquire basic reading and counting skills sooner.
swaps.note: Acquire / develop + skills or knowledge.

swaps.plainSentence: Structured learning is also said to be good for children from disadvantaged homes.
swaps.formalSentence: Structured learning is also said to be beneficial for children from disadvantaged homes.

traps.why: wrong word: a beneficiary is a person

swaps.note: 'Good for' → beneficial for / advantageous for.

swaps.plainSentence: So, they argue, delaying school wastes valuable learning time.
swaps.formalSentence: Consequently, they argue, delaying school wastes valuable learning time.

traps.why: needs an -ing clause, not a sentence

swaps.note: Show the result the first group predicts.

swaps.plainSentence: Children who start late may be behind their peers in other countries.
swaps.formalSentence: Children who start late may lag behind their peers in other countries.
swaps.note: Lag behind / fall behind + peers / competitors.

formal: On the other hand, others argue
swaps.plainSentence: But other people say that young children need time to play.
swaps.formalSentence: Conversely, others maintain that young children need time to play.

traps.why: contradicts a statement; not for views

traps.text: On the other side, others say

swaps.note: Open Body 2 by switching clearly to the opposite view.

swaps.plainSentence: People who are against this claim that formal lessons can damage a child's natural curiosity.
swaps.formalSentence: Critics of this approach claim that formal lessons can damage a child's natural curiosity.

traps.why: adjective phrase cannot be the subject

swaps.note: Critics / opponents name the second group precisely.

swaps.plainSentence: Too much pressure at a young age can stop creativity.
swaps.formalSentence: Too much pressure at a young age can stifle creativity.
swaps.note: Stifle collocates with creativity, curiosity and innovation.

swaps.plainSentence: And children who are pushed too early may lose interest in learning altogether.
swaps.formalSentence: In addition, children who are pushed too early may lose interest in learning altogether.
swaps.note: Avoid starting a formal sentence with 'And'.

swaps.plainSentence: The success of Finland, where school begins at seven, means that a late start does no harm.
swaps.formalSentence: The success of Finland, where school begins at seven, suggests that a late start does no harm.
swaps.note: Hedge claims drawn from a single example.

swaps.plainSentence: In their view, free play is really important for social and emotional development.
swaps.formalSentence: In their view, free play is essential for social and emotional development.
swaps.note: No 'very' or 'really' before absolute adjectives.

swaps.plainSentence: Children learn a lot of skills through play, such as cooperation and problem-solving.
swaps.formalSentence: Children learn a wide range of skills through play, such as cooperation and problem-solving.
swaps.note: A wide range of + plural noun shows variety.

swaps.plainSentence: All in all, while early schooling has some benefits, a later start seems wiser.
swaps.formalSentence: On balance, while early schooling has some benefits, a later start seems wiser.

traps.why: wrong phrase: not a conclusion linker

swaps.note: 'On balance' weighs both views: perfect for discussion essays.

swaps.plainSentence: Having considered both sides, I think that children should not start formal lessons before the age of six.
swaps.formalSentence: Having considered both sides, I remain convinced that children should not start formal lessons before the age of six.
swaps.note: Restate the view you gave in the introduction.

swaps.plainSentence: Parents and teachers should make sure that the early years focus on play rather than tests.
swaps.formalSentence: Parents and teachers should ensure that the early years focus on play rather than tests.
swaps.note: Ensure (make certain) ≠ assure (promise) ≠ insure (insurance).

swaps.plainSentence: The ideal approach may be a mix of play and gentle instruction.
swaps.formalSentence: The ideal approach may be a combination of play and gentle instruction.
swaps.note: Suggest a compromise to end a discussion essay.

rewrites.plain: Some people think children should start school early but other people disagree.
rewrites.best: Opinions are divided on whether children should begin formal education at an early age.
rewrites.tooPlain: Some people think children should start school early, but others disagree.
rewrites.broken: Opinions are dividing about if children should begin formal education early.

rewrites.plain: This essay will talk about both sides and then I will say what I think.
rewrites.best: This essay will examine both perspectives before explaining why I favour the latter.
rewrites.tooPlain: This essay will discuss both sides and then give my opinion.
rewrites.tooPlainWhy: correct but does not preview your view
rewrites.broken: This essay will discuss about both sides and I will tell my opinion.
rewrites.brokenWhy: 'discuss about' and 'tell my opinion' are wrong

rewrites.plain: People who like early school say kids learn really fast.
rewrites.best: Proponents of early schooling contend that young children absorb new information remarkably quickly.
rewrites.tooPlain: People who support early school say children learn very fast.
rewrites.broken: Proponents for early schooling contend that young children absorbs information remarkable quickly.

rewrites.plain: So they think waiting until seven wastes time.
rewrites.best: Consequently, they argue that delaying formal education until the age of seven wastes valuable learning time.
rewrites.tooPlain: So they think that waiting until seven is a waste of time.
rewrites.broken: Consequently, they argue delaying formal education until seven is wasting of valuable time.

rewrites.plain: But other people say too much school stops kids being creative.
rewrites.best: Conversely, critics maintain that excessive academic pressure at a young age can stifle creativity.
rewrites.tooPlain: However, other people say that too much school stops creativity.
rewrites.broken: On the contrary, critics maintain that excessive pressure can stifle the creative of children.

rewrites.plain: In Finland school starts at seven and it is fine.
rewrites.best: In Finland, for instance, formal schooling begins at seven, yet academic standards remain among the highest in Europe.
rewrites.tooPlain: For example, in Finland school starts at seven and the results are good.
rewrites.broken: Such as Finland, school begins at seven, yet the standards remains high.

rewrites.plain: In the end, I think the second group is more right.
rewrites.best: On balance, I would maintain that the latter view is more convincing.
rewrites.tooPlain: In conclusion, I think the second view is better.
rewrites.broken: On balance, I would maintain that the later view is more convinced.

report.question: Some people believe that children should start formal education at a very early age, while others think they should not begin school until they are at least seven years old. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

steps.prompt: Paraphrase the question and show two sides
steps.best: Opinions are divided on the question of when children should begin formal schooling, with some favouring an early start and others arguing that it should be delayed until around the age of seven.

others.text: Some people believe that children should start formal education at a very early age, while others disagree.
Nowadays, education is a very important topic in the modern world.
others.why: cliché; says nothing about the question

steps.prompt: Outline the essay and give your view
steps.best: This essay will examine both perspectives, but I would argue that a later start, preceded by play-based learning, is more beneficial for the majority of children.

others.text: I will talk about both sides and then say what I think.
This essay will discuss about both views and I am agree with the second.

steps.best: On the one hand, proponents of early schooling contend that young children absorb new information remarkably quickly and should therefore be taught to read and count as soon as possible.

others.text: On one side, some people think children learn fast so they should go to school early.
others.why: 'on one side' is wrong; plain wording

others.text: Firstly, proponents of early schooling are contending that children absorbs knowledge fast.

steps.best: Their rationale is that pupils who acquire basic literacy and numeracy skills at an early age will have a firm foundation for all their later learning.

others.text: The reason is because children who learn early do better later.
Their rational is that pupils obtain literacies earlier and have firm foundation.

steps.best: Moreover, early schooling is often said to be particularly beneficial for children from disadvantaged backgrounds, who might otherwise fall behind their more privileged peers.

others.text: Also, it is good for poor children so they are not behind rich children.
Moreover, early schooling is beneficial for children from disadvantage backgrounds.

steps.best: Conversely, critics of this approach maintain that formal lessons at the age of four or five can stifle children's natural curiosity and cause them unnecessary stress.

others.text: On the contrary, other people say that school is too stressful for small kids.
Conversely, critics maintain that formal lessons can stifle the curious of children.

steps.best: They point to countries such as Finland, where formal schooling does not begin until the age of seven, as evidence that a later start does not harm academic achievement.

others.text: For example, in Finland they start at seven and they are OK.
Such as Finland, where school begins at seven, the results are not harmed.

steps.best: In their view, unstructured play is essential for developing the social and emotional skills, such as cooperation and resilience, that underpin successful learning in later years.

others.text: They think playing is very important for children's feelings and making friends.
In their view, play is very essential for developing social skills that underpins learning.

steps.best: In conclusion, while there are valid arguments for introducing academic lessons early, the evidence suggests that young children benefit more from learning through play.

others.text: In the end, both sides are right in some ways.
In conclusion, early and late start both has advantages.

steps.best: I would therefore maintain that formal education should begin at around six or seven, provided that the preceding years offer a rich and stimulating environment.

others.text: So I think kids should start school at seven.
I would therefore maintain that school should begin at seven, provided the years before offers rich environment.

topics.title: Advantages and disadvantages
topics.blurb: Weigh the benefits against the drawbacks and say which side wins.

swaps.plainSentence: In recent years, more and more people have started to work from home.
swaps.formalSentence: In recent years, an increasing number of people have started to work from home.
swaps.note: 'More and more' is spoken; use 'an increasing number of'.

swaps.plainSentence: This thing has been made possible by high-speed internet connections.
swaps.formalSentence: This trend has been made possible by high-speed internet connections.
swaps.note: Refer back with 'this trend / development', never 'this thing'.

swaps.plainSentence: Working from home has both good and bad points.
swaps.formalSentence: Working from home has both benefits and drawbacks.
swaps.note: Name both sides in the introduction.

swaps.plainSentence: I believe that the benefits are more than the drawbacks.
swaps.formalSentence: I believe that the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
swaps.note: Answer 'Do the advantages outweigh…?' directly in the thesis.

swaps.plainSentence: I would argue that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages for most people.
swaps.formalSentence: I would argue that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages for the majority of workers.
swaps.note: Qualify your claim: 'for the majority of …'.

swaps.plainSentence: The main good thing about working from home is the time it saves.
swaps.formalSentence: The principal advantage of working from home is the time it saves.
swaps.note: Principal (main) ≠ principle (a rule).

swaps.plainSentence: Remote workers no longer have to travel to work every day.
swaps.formalSentence: Remote workers no longer have to commute daily.
swaps.note: Commute = travel regularly between home and work.

formal: reduce their expenditure on office space
cut their spending on office space
swaps.plainSentence: Companies can also spend less money on offices.
swaps.formalSentence: Companies can also reduce their expenditure on office space.
swaps.note: Expenditure on + noun (a formal noun for spending).

swaps.plainSentence: Flexible hours help parents to combine work and childcare.
swaps.formalSentence: Flexible hours enable parents to combine work and childcare.
swaps.note: Enable / allow + person + to do.

swaps.plainSentence: Many workers say they feel less stressed when they work at home.
swaps.formalSentence: Many workers report lower levels of stress when they work at home.
swaps.note: Report + noun sounds objective and academic.

swaps.plainSentence: Because of this, productivity often rises rather than falls.
swaps.formalSentence: As a result, productivity often rises rather than falls.
swaps.note: End Body 1 with the positive result.

swaps.plainSentence: Studies suggest that many remote employees work better without office distractions.
swaps.formalSentence: Studies suggest that many remote employees are more productive without office distractions.
swaps.note: 'Productive' names exactly what 'better' means here.

swaps.plainSentence: But remote working is not without its problems.
swaps.formalSentence: However, remote working is not without its problems.

traps.why: joins two clauses in one sentence

swaps.note: Turn to the disadvantages with a clear signal.

swaps.plainSentence: The most serious bad point is the risk of loneliness.
swaps.formalSentence: The most serious drawback is the risk of loneliness.
swaps.note: 'Bad point' → drawback / disadvantage.

swaps.plainSentence: Without colleagues around them, some employees feel lonely and unmotivated.
swaps.formalSentence: Without colleagues around them, some employees become socially isolated and unmotivated.
swaps.note: -ed = the person's feeling; -ing = the cause.

swaps.plainSentence: Working at the kitchen table mixes up work and family life.
swaps.formalSentence: Working at the kitchen table blurs the boundary between work and family life.
swaps.note: Blur the boundary between A and B.

swaps.plainSentence: Communication within teams can get worse when meetings take place only online.
swaps.formalSentence: Communication within teams can deteriorate when meetings take place only online.
swaps.note: Deteriorate is intransitive: things deteriorate.

swaps.plainSentence: It can also be difficult for bosses to monitor staff performance.
swaps.formalSentence: It can also be difficult for managers to monitor staff performance.
swaps.note: 'Boss' is informal; use manager or employer.

swaps.plainSentence: This lack of face-to-face contact is a big problem for new staff.
swaps.formalSentence: This lack of face-to-face contact poses a serious challenge for new staff.
swaps.note: Pose / present a challenge (to / for someone).

swaps.plainSentence: In the end, I believe that remote working is a positive development.
swaps.formalSentence: On balance, I believe that remote working is a positive development.

traps.why: introduces a final point, not a verdict

swaps.note: 'On balance' = after weighing both sides.

swaps.plainSentence: Despite its limitations, working from home is a good thing for most employees.
swaps.formalSentence: Despite its limitations, working from home is a positive development for most employees.
swaps.note: Give a clear final verdict on the trend.

swaps.plainSentence: Most of these problems can be fixed if companies hold regular team meetings.
swaps.formalSentence: Most of these problems can be overcome if companies hold regular team meetings.
swaps.note: Show that the drawbacks can be managed.

swaps.plainSentence: With good management, the benefits for both employers and employees would increase a lot.
swaps.formalSentence: With good management, the benefits for both employers and employees would increase considerably.
swaps.note: 'A lot' is spoken English; use considerably.

rewrites.plain: Nowadays more and more people work from home and this has good and bad points.
rewrites.best: In recent years, an increasing number of people have begun working from home, a trend that has both benefits and drawbacks.
rewrites.tooPlain: Nowadays, many people work from home, and this has advantages and disadvantages.

report.question: In many countries, a growing number of people now work from home rather than travelling to an office. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

others.text: The main good thing is that people don't have to travel to work.

topics.title: Problems and solutions
topics.blurb: Explain the causes of a problem, then propose realistic ways to tackle it.

swaps.plainSentence: The growing volume of household waste has become a big problem in many cities.
swaps.formalSentence: The growing volume of household waste has become a pressing issue in many cities.
swaps.note: 'Pressing' = urgent, needing action now.

swaps.plainSentence: Urban households are producing more and more rubbish each year.
swaps.formalSentence: Urban households are producing ever-increasing amounts of waste each year.
swaps.note: Amount / quantity + uncountable nouns like waste.

formal: a number of possible remedies for it
swaps.plainSentence: This essay will outline the main causes of this trend and suggest some ways to fix it.
swaps.formalSentence: This essay will outline the main causes of this trend and suggest several measures to address it.

traps.text: several measures to address with it

swaps.note: Measures / remedies are the key nouns for solutions.

swaps.plainSentence: I believe that the problem mainly comes from modern consumer habits.
swaps.formalSentence: I believe that the problem mainly stems from modern consumer habits.
swaps.note: Stem from / arise from introduce the root cause.

swaps.plainSentence: However, it can be sorted out through a combination of government action and individual effort.
swaps.formalSentence: However, it can be tackled through a combination of government action and individual effort.
swaps.note: Tackle / address a problem: formal, active-sounding verbs.

swaps.plainSentence: The main reason for this problem is the culture of convenience that dominates modern life.
swaps.formalSentence: The primary cause of this problem is the culture of convenience that dominates modern life.
swaps.note: Cause of / reason for: learn the prepositions.

swaps.plainSentence: Much of this waste is caused by excessive packaging.
swaps.formalSentence: Much of this waste can be attributed to excessive packaging.
swaps.note: X can be attributed to Y = Y is the cause.

swaps.plainSentence: Consumers now throw away items that could easily be repaired.
swaps.formalSentence: Consumers now discard items that could easily be repaired.
swaps.note: Dispose of / discard: formal verbs for 'throw away'.

swaps.plainSentence: People buy far more goods than they actually need.
swaps.formalSentence: People purchase far more goods than they actually need.
swaps.note: 'Purchase' suits formal essays and letters alike.

swaps.plainSentence: Cheap, low-quality products have to be replaced frequently.
swaps.formalSentence: Inexpensive, low-quality products have to be replaced frequently.
swaps.note: Economical = saving money; economic = about the economy.

swaps.plainSentence: The rapid growth of online shopping makes the situation worse.
swaps.formalSentence: The rapid growth of online shopping exacerbates the situation.
swaps.note: Close Body 1 with a factor that intensifies the problem.

swaps.plainSentence: Almost every delivery arrives wrapped in lots of cardboard and plastic.
swaps.formalSentence: Almost every delivery arrives wrapped in vast quantities of cardboard and plastic.
swaps.note: Quantities / amounts for materials; numbers for countable items.

swaps.plainSentence: One way to fix this is to make manufacturers responsible for their packaging.
swaps.formalSentence: One viable solution is to make manufacturers responsible for their packaging.
swaps.note: Open Body 2 with your first solution.

formal: It is incumbent upon governments to
swaps.plainSentence: The government should introduce stricter recycling targets for every district.
swaps.formalSentence: It is incumbent upon governments to introduce stricter recycling targets for every district.

traps.text: It is incumbent for governments to

swaps.note: 'It is incumbent upon X to…' = X has a duty to.

swaps.plainSentence: Authorities could make laws to limit single-use plastics.
swaps.formalSentence: Authorities could introduce legislation to limit single-use plastics.
swaps.note: Introduce / pass legislation; legislation has no plural.

swaps.plainSentence: Charging for plastic bags has helped to stop their overuse in several countries.
swaps.formalSentence: Charging for plastic bags has helped to curb their overuse in several countries.
swaps.note: Curb / curtail = limit something harmful.

swaps.plainSentence: Local councils could also punish households that do not separate their rubbish.
swaps.formalSentence: Local councils could also penalise households that do not separate their rubbish.
swaps.note: British spelling: penalise; impose fines on + someone.

swaps.plainSentence: Schools and the media should teach people about the environmental cost of waste.
swaps.formalSentence: Schools and the media should raise public awareness of the environmental cost of waste.
swaps.note: Raise (transitive) awareness; prices rise (intransitive).

swaps.plainSentence: Deposit schemes for bottles make people want to return them.
swaps.formalSentence: Deposit schemes for bottles give people an incentive to return them.
swaps.note: Incentives are a classic solution word.

swaps.plainSentence: Together, such measures would make things better within a few years.
swaps.formalSentence: Together, such measures would alleviate the problem within a few years.
swaps.note: Alleviate problems; enhance good things.

swaps.plainSentence: Finally, the rise in household waste has identifiable causes and practical solutions.
swaps.formalSentence: In conclusion, the rise in household waste has identifiable causes and practical solutions.

traps.why: lists a final point, not a conclusion

swaps.note: 'Finally' introduces a last point, not a conclusion.

swaps.plainSentence: The increase in household waste is mostly because of overconsumption and excessive packaging.
swaps.formalSentence: The increase in household waste is largely the result of overconsumption and excessive packaging.

traps.why: needs a clause, not a noun

swaps.note: Summarise the causes in one sentence.

swaps.plainSentence: If nothing is done, the problem will soon overwhelm existing landfill sites.
swaps.formalSentence: If left unchecked, the problem will soon overwhelm existing landfill sites.
swaps.note: Warn of consequences to end strongly.

swaps.plainSentence: Overconsumption will have bad results for the planet and its future inhabitants.
swaps.formalSentence: Overconsumption will have serious repercussions for the planet and its future inhabitants.
swaps.note: Repercussions = serious, often unexpected effects.

rewrites.plain: Nowadays rubbish is a big problem in cities.
rewrites.best: In recent years, the growing volume of household waste has become a pressing issue in many cities.
rewrites.tooPlain: Nowadays, rubbish is a serious problem in cities.
rewrites.broken: In recent years, the growing volume of household wastes has become a pressed issue.

rewrites.plain: The main reason is people buy too much stuff.

rewrites.plain: Online shopping makes it worse because of all the boxes.

rewrites.broken: The growth of online shopping has exaggerated the problem owing to the large number of packaging.

rewrites.plain: The government should make laws to stop plastic.
rewrites.best: It is incumbent upon governments to introduce legislation that curbs the use of single-use plastics.
rewrites.tooPlain: The government should make new laws to stop plastic bags.
rewrites.broken: It is incumbent for governments to introduce legislations that curve plastic use.

rewrites.plain: People should be punished if they don't recycle.

rewrites.tooPlain: People who don't recycle should be punished.
rewrites.broken: Households that fail to recycle could be penaltied through modest fines.

rewrites.plain: Schools should teach people about rubbish so things get better.
rewrites.best: Schools should raise awareness of the environmental cost of waste, which would help to alleviate the problem.
rewrites.tooPlain: Schools should teach children about waste so the problem gets better.
rewrites.broken: Schools should rise awareness of the cost of waste, which would help to enhance the problem.

rewrites.plain: If nothing is done, it will be really bad for the future.
rewrites.best: If left unchecked, this trend will have serious repercussions for future generations.
rewrites.tooPlain: If nothing is done, it will be very bad for future generations.

others.text: The main reason is that people like easy things and throw them away.

topics.title: Formal letter
topics.blurb: Complaints, requests and applications: polite, precise and never chatty.

swaps.plainSentence: Hi,
swaps.formalSentence: Dear Sir or Madam,

traps.why: slang: never in a formal letter

swaps.note: Name unknown → 'Dear Sir or Madam' → 'Yours faithfully'.

swaps.plainSentence: Hello Mr Patel,
swaps.formalSentence: Dear Mr Patel,
swaps.note: Name known → 'Dear Mr/Ms + surname' → 'Yours sincerely'.

swaps.plainSentence: I want to complain about a coffee machine that I bought from your store.
swaps.formalSentence: I am writing to complain about a coffee machine that I bought from your store.
swaps.note: State your purpose in the very first sentence.

formal: I would like to apply for the position of
I wish to apply for the post of
swaps.plainSentence: I want the job of assistant manager that was advertised in the Evening Post.
swaps.formalSentence: I would like to apply for the position of assistant manager that was advertised in the Evening Post.

traps.text: I would like to apply to the position of
I am applying the job of

swaps.note: Application letters: apply for the position / post of.

swaps.plainSentence: I am writing about the recent changes to the parking arrangements at our building.
swaps.formalSentence: I am writing regarding the recent changes to the parking arrangements at our building.

traps.why: 'regards' is a closing, not a preposition

swaps.note: Regarding / with regard to introduce the topic of a letter.

swaps.plainSentence: I got the machine from your Riverside branch on 3 March.
swaps.formalSentence: I purchased the machine from your Riverside branch on 3 March.

traps.why: no present perfect with a date

swaps.note: Give exact dates and places in a complaint.

swaps.plainSentence: Unfortunately, the machine doesn't work properly.
swaps.formalSentence: Unfortunately, the machine does not function correctly.
swaps.note: Avoid contractions in formal letters: does not, I am.

swaps.plainSentence: On 5 March, I rang the shop to report the fault.
swaps.formalSentence: On 5 March, I telephoned your store to report the fault.
swaps.note: Contact / telephone + object directly.

formal: gave me an assurance that they would
swaps.plainSentence: A member of staff said they would send a technician within two days.
swaps.formalSentence: A member of staff assured me that they would send a technician within two days.
swaps.note: Assure someone that…: a firm promise.

formal: the matter was not followed up
swaps.plainSentence: However, nothing happened.
swaps.formalSentence: However, no action was taken.
swaps.note: The passive sounds objective: 'no action was taken'.

swaps.plainSentence: I am very disappointed with the bad service I have received.
swaps.formalSentence: I am very disappointed with the unsatisfactory service I have received.

traps.why: people are unsatisfied; service is unsatisfactory

swaps.note: Unsatisfactory (the service) ≠ dissatisfied (the customer).

swaps.plainSentence: I am really angry about the way my complaint has been handled.
swaps.formalSentence: I am extremely dissatisfied with the way my complaint has been handled.
swaps.note: Express displeasure firmly but politely.

swaps.plainSentence: Sorry for any inconvenience my late payment may have caused.
swaps.formalSentence: I apologise for any inconvenience my late payment may have caused.
swaps.note: Formal apologies: I apologise for / Please accept my apologies.

formal: provide me with a full refund
swaps.plainSentence: I would like you to give me my money back.
swaps.formalSentence: I would like you to provide me with a full refund.
swaps.note: Refund / reimburse already mean 'give money back'.

swaps.plain: change it for a new one
formal: replace it with a new model
exchange it for a new model
swaps.plainSentence: Alternatively, you could change it for a new one.
swaps.formalSentence: Alternatively, you could replace it with a new model.

traps.text: replace it for a new model
substitute it by a new model

swaps.note: Replace X with Y; exchange X for Y.

swaps.plainSentence: I trust that you will fix the problem promptly.
swaps.formalSentence: I trust that you will rectify the situation promptly.
swaps.note: Rectify / resolve: formal verbs for 'fix'.

formal: I would be grateful if you could contact me
I would appreciate it if you could contact me
swaps.plainSentence: Please call me on 07700 900123 to arrange a visit.
swaps.formalSentence: I would be grateful if you could contact me on 07700 900123 to arrange a visit.

traps.text: I would be grateful if you can contact me
I would be grateful that you contact me

swaps.note: A polite request softens even a firm complaint.

swaps.plainSentence: I would appreciate a reply asap.
swaps.formalSentence: I would appreciate a reply at your earliest convenience.
swaps.note: Never use abbreviations like asap in a formal letter.

swaps.plainSentence: Please tell me what action you intend to take.
swaps.formalSentence: Please inform me what action you intend to take.
swaps.note: Inform / advise me of…, inform me what…

formal: I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward to your reply.
swaps.plainSentence: Write back soon.
swaps.formalSentence: I look forward to hearing from you.

traps.text: I am looking forward to hear from you.
I look forward to hear from you.

swaps.note: 'Look forward to' + -ing: the 'to' is a preposition.

swaps.plainSentence: Bye,
swaps.formalSentence: Yours faithfully,
swaps.note: Dear Sir or Madam → Yours faithfully.

swaps.plainSentence: Thanks,
swaps.formalSentence: Yours sincerely,
swaps.note: Dear Mr Patel → Yours sincerely.

report.question:
A friend has invited you to spend a weekend with them next month, but you are unable to go. Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• thank your friend for the invitation
• explain why you cannot go
• suggest another time when you could visit
Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses. Begin your letter as follows: Dear ……………,
